title: Advanced Selectors and Combinators
description: Using complex selectors and combinators to target elements precisely in CSS.

flashcards.question: What is an attribute selector?
flashcards.answer: A selector that targets elements based on attribute values, e.g., [type='text'].

flashcards.question: What does the child combinator (>) do?
flashcards.answer: Selects direct children of an element.

flashcards.question: How does the descendant combinator (space) work?
flashcards.answer: Selects all descendants of an element, at any level.

flashcards.question: What is the adjacent sibling combinator (+)?
flashcards.answer: Selects the element immediately following another sibling.

flashcards.question: What does the general sibling combinator (~) select?
flashcards.answer: All siblings after the first element that share the same parent.

flashcards.question: How can you select the last child of a parent?
What does the :not() selector do?
flashcards.answer: Selects elements that do NOT match the specified selector.
